key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.حَيَّاكَ اللَّهُ: May Allah keep you alive (a common greeting)
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (a legal ruling indicating preference against an action)

ai.seo_question: What is the disliked practice regarding the greeting 'May Allah keep you alive' in Shia etiquette?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on the completeness and reciprocity of social greetings, warning against the abruptness of saying 'Hayyak Allah' without following up with 'As-salamu alaykum'. It reflects the broader Islamic principle that greetings are a form of worship and social bonding, requiring full attention and completion to avoid appearing dismissive or incomplete. The ruling underscores the importance of maintaining dignified and warm interpersonal relations as prescribed by the Imams.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> disliked it for the man that he should be saying, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you alive’, then he is silent, without offering the greetings of peace’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘It is undesirable for a man to say, “May Allah keep you living,” then remain silent without offering the greeting of peace thereafter.’”
